## Outcome

PR #306 merged after I kept the change limited to redundant selector checks. Two CI pull requests also closed after review, but not for the same reason: one solution was more complicated than necessary, while the other fix belonged in a different project.

## Context

PR #306 began before GSoC. This week I completed its focused review and merge without turning it into a behavior change.

## What I Did

- Merged [PR #306](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/306) on June 29 without changing selector behavior.
- Closed [PR #338](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/338) because its skip logic was more complex than the maintainer’s preferred solution: remove the GitHub Pages test for fork PRs.
- Closed [PR #341](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/341) because the maintainer considered the fix to belong in `atime`, not Animint2.
- Updated [PR #339](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/339) with the current upstream changes.

## Learnings

Closing two branches after spending time debugging them was disappointing. The review was still useful and specific: one patch was too complicated, and the other was in the wrong repository.

## Challenges / Notes

The closures did not erase the debugging work, but they changed what I should do next. I did not replace either public explanation with a vague “not preferred” label.

## Next Week Targets

Use the midterm checkpoint to decide which remaining branches I could realistically finish.
